tools_used: WebFetch of a supremecourt.gov docket PDF
helpful: The statpack interim section's per-Term counts made the strictly-prior pool arithmetic straightforward.
CourtListener docket entries for the Ninth Circuit appeal gave the panel composition and the 'subject to reconsideration by the merits panel' language, which the application's own summary did not.
gaps: fedcourts query with --include-applications ranks time-extension applications first by recency; a filter for application_kind=substantive would make the priors sweep useful.
No conditioned interim cut (state applicant, response requested) exists, so the class adjustment rests on the predictor's own read of practice.
The response brief that opens a response-filed event is not provisioned; every predictor has to fetch and OCR it itself.
notes: WebFetch could not read the PDF's text but saved the binary; pypdf from the project environment extracted it cleanly.
